clue.text: Tree, a sure thing to be cut down

indicators.note: cutting down a word shortens it by trimming its final letter

parts.note: a cert is a racing term for a certainty

explanation.surface: A forester decides that a tree is certain to be felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cut down' lops the last letter off A CERT, leaving four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple genus is named Acer, so this is a botanical name for a kind of tree.

clue.text: Study part of church plan

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a spire is the tapering top of a church tower

explanation.surface: Someone examines part of a church's design drawings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plan' looks like a noun completing 'church plan', but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot secretly together is to scheme, so the verb sense of plan fits.

clue.text: Refer back to Carter after a review

indicators.note: a review reworks things, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A historian sends readers back to President Carter after reviewing him.
explanation.definitionFit: To act retrospectively is to apply to or bear on the past, so it refers back in time.

clue.text: Blimey, Action Man toy people!

definitions.note: the clue names the company rather than a single toy

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey
Action Man is a toy soldier, and a soldier can be a GI

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in delight at the makers of a toy soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Action Man was a British toy soldier figure (the US original was GI Joe). Corgi is a British firm famous for die-cast model cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Corgi Toys is a British manufacturer of die-cast model vehicles, so its makers are toy people.

clue.text: European composer's audible reminder

indicators.note: audible tells us to go by the sound of the words

parts.note: Czech Liszt: a Czech is a European, and Liszt a composer

explanation.surface: A tune by a European composer serves as a spoken memory aid.
explanation.walkthrough: Liszt was actually Hungarian, but 'Czech Liszt' only needs to sound right.
explanation.definitionFit: A written list of items to tick off acts as a prompt to memory.

clue.text: Disproof of Urdu concept ends certified cases

indicators.note: cases is a verb here: encloses or surrounds

parts.note: certified means genuine, real

indicators.note: the ends of these three words are their final letters

explanation.surface: A disproof of some Urdu idea ends up in certified case files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes F, U and T from 'of Urdu concept', and 'cases' puts REAL around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal proving something false is the noun form of disproving.

clue.text: Drinking house has attractive quality, do you not think?

parts.note: an inn is a pub
it is sex appeal or charm

explanation.surface: Someone asks for agreement that the pub has charm.
explanation.definitionFit: This British street contraction of 'isn't it' is a tag question seeking agreement.

clue.text: Instant account

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'back in a ...'

explanation.walkthrough: To buy 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British senses: a very short moment, and credit given by a shopkeeper.

clue.text: Russian city in the direction of capital, less popular

parts.note: to means towards

indicators.note: less means without, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: Minsk is the capital of Belarus
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Heading towards a capital but with less popularity, in a Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' takes IN out of MINSK, leaving MSK.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large Siberian city founded in 1604.

clue.text: Function in garden is occasionally set up

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A garden is sometimes laid out for a social function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reads upwards in a down clue, turning ENISOC around.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry it is a standard mathematical function of an angle.

clue.text: Funny old picture: father in one, it's inferred?

parts.note: the words father in one, rearranged, spell the first two words of the film title; a mess is what jumbles them

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether someone has become a father.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: the letters of FATHER IN ONE put in a mess give the first two words. That anagram signal is what 'it's inferred' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1930 Laurel and Hardy short, an old comedy film.

clue.text: Wheel, let me add, turning on missile

indicators.note: turning round tells us to read the postscript letters backwards

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is how a letter writer adds an afterthought
a rocket is a missile

explanation.surface: A speaker interjects that a wheel is spinning on a missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' turns PS into SP.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed wheel engaging a chain, as on a bicycle, is the cogged kind meant here.

clue.text: Reminder from 18?

definitions.meaning: a keepsake or souvenir that brings something to mind
18 is Barbie, whose boyfriend is Ken

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as TO KEN: the tag on a present from Barbie to her doll boyfriend Ken.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake given in remembrance is a memento, so serves as a reminder.

clue.text: List extraordinarily sexy parts with old toy

indicators.note: racy parts the shuffled letters, sitting between them
something done extraordinarily is out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: racy means risqué or sexy
and means together with

explanation.surface: An instruction to list the saucy bits along with an old toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinarily' rearranges the clue's List, and 'parts' means the sexy word sits between its letters. Tracy Island is the Thunderbirds base, a 1990s toy playset.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderbirds' island base was a famously hard-to-find 1990s toy playset, now a nostalgic collectible.

clue.text: Last seen of halcyon days, once winds blow

indicators.note: the last seen of a word is its final letter
winds as a verb means twists, so these letters are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: Wistful farewell to happy days, when the winds blew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' looks like what winds do; it is slang for cocaine. 'winds' rearranges DAYS ONCE into OSECANDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang names for cocaine, the drug taken by snorting.

clue.text: Said Irish county inspired by half-hearted deed

indicators.note: breathed in by, so the county goes inside
half its heart is lost, so one of the middle pair of letters goes

parts.note: taken as written
Clare is a county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: A half-hearted act is said to be inspired by an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of the two middle letters of deed, and 'inspired by' puts the county inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something formally is to have said it, past tense matching past tense.

clue.text: For songwriter, insert fish?

parts.note: read the word insert as in plus sert: the fish called a chub goes in the letters that follow in

explanation.surface: A request to add a fish for a songwriter, perhaps a nod to his Trout Quintet.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a playful instruction: split 'insert' as IN + SERT and put the fish IN SERT. Some solvers objected that SERT is not a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer wrote over six hundred Lieder, so he is a great writer of songs.

clue.text: Old toy, among other things, contains boat

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and other things
has means holds or contains
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: An old toy, among other items, holds a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: This drawing screen with two knobs is a classic childhood toy from the 1960s onward.

clue.text: Proceed inside frightful haunt, familiar place

indicators.note: inside says the verb goes within the rearranged letters
frightful means dreadful, so the letters are put into disorder

parts.note: go means proceed

explanation.surface: Someone presses on into a frightening haunted spot that feels familiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' shuffles haunt, and 'inside' puts the verb within it. 'haunt' looks like the definition, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A place one habitually visits to relax is a regular spot one knows well.

clue.text: Australian gathering toy

definitions.meaning: Australian slang for a barbecue party
the famous fashion doll made by Mattel

explanation.definitionFit: Australians call a barbecue get-together by this name, which is also that of a fashion doll.

clue.text: Tea in a state, knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the state's letters are read backwards

parts.note: Mass is the abbreviation for Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Tea spilt by someone in a flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns MASS into SSAM. 'in a state' looks like an idiom for being upset; here it is a link word plus A plus the state.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong black tea is grown in the north-east Indian region of the same name.

clue.text: Toy sensually at first with this organ

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: the Indy is a nickname for The Independent, the newspaper printing this puzzle

explanation.surface: A suggestive remark about playing with a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks like music or anatomy but means a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: This British fashion doll was a rival to Barbie from the 1960s.

clue.text: Children's author not entirely captivating a European city

indicators.note: captivating holds something captive inside
not entirely means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: A. A. Milne wrote Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: A children's writer, not wholly charming, goes to a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims MILNE to MILN, and 'captivating' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital of Lombardy in northern Italy.

clue.text: Lovely short 18 for old Australian driver

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: nice means lovely
18 is Barbie, and the old bearer of that surname was Klaus Barbie, the Nazi war criminal

explanation.surface: A sweet, brief tribute to an old Australian golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 18-down is BARBIE; once, that name meant Klaus Barbie, the Gestapo officer. 'Australian' looks like a setter's slip: Jack Nicklaus is American, as blog commenters noted.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer hits long tee shots with the club called a driver, so a golf great is a driver.

clue.text: Nun observed performing with flea, jumping easily?

indicators.note: performing suggests acting out, so these letters are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A nun is watched putting on a show with a flea that jumps easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' looks like part of the anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone very anxious and edgy is startled at the slightest thing, so jumps easily.

clue.text: Bank manager's back, see

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A bank manager returns to look at something.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely in Cambridgeshire is the classic crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to count on or depend on them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Fruity bananas

definitions.meaning: tasting rich or full of kernels, like a flavour of wine or cake

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is flavour, full of kernel-like richness; the other is slang for mad, as is bananas.

clue.text: See fruit

definitions.meaning: to see someone is to go out with them romantically
the sweet brown fruit of a palm

explanation.definitionFit: To go out romantically with someone, and the sticky fruit of a palm tree, share one spelling.
